data.name: Sadeep
data.gender_notes: Sadeep is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Sadeep is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Sad' which means 'deep' and 'Deep' meaning 'wisdom'. This name is for a baby boy born near a deep body of water, symbolizing the depth of knowledge and wisdom that the baby is expected to acquire in life. The name Sadeep carries the meaning “Deep, Wise” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Sadeep usually hope their child will grow to embody deep, wise and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: The name Sadeep holds deep spiritual significance as it symbolizes the pursuit of knowledge and wisdom, just as the deep waters represent the vastness of the universe and the mysteries it holds.
data.etymology: Sadeep belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Deep, Wise.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Sadeep total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

historical_references.reference: Sadeep is mentioned in the epic Mahabharata, as the name of a king of Haihayas or Vatsa dynasty who ruled in the region of Mathura in northern India during the Mahabharata war (circa 3100-2900 BCE).
historical_references.context: Hindu mythology, Mahabharata war, northern India, Mathura region, Haihayas or Vatsa dynasty, king of Mathura

historical_references.reference: Another reference to Sadeep is found in the Purana text, Harivamsa, where he is described as a son of Vishvamitra, a famous sage who was also the father of Laxmana, the younger brother of Lord Rama. Sadeep is said to have ruled over the region of Sauvira in western India during the Treta Yuga (circa 2400-1900 BCE).
